title: Private deploy networking — incident breadcrumbs (VPC peering / DNS / TLS / egress)
content:
Summary:
- Short: customer private deployment lost connectivity to model-serving cluster after network maintenance window. Symptoms: API requests time out or hit TLS handshake errors; internal healthchecks to model nodes flaky.
- Affects one customer VPC peered to our private deployment VPC in us-west-2.
- Working hypothesis (top-of-head): route propagation for VPC peering missing / partial, plus DNS fallback returning public IPs; secondary issue: TLS connections failing when requests route through a NAT/egress path that rewrites SNI (weird).

Timeline & quick notes:
- 2026-02-18 02:05 UTC — maintenance window: applied route-table cleanup in infra account (PR #221).
- 2026-02-18 03:40 UTC — first customer alert: 502 / TLS handshake fail; traces show connection resets.
- 2026-02-18 04:10 UTC — rolled back one route change; partial recovery for some control-plane traffic.
- 2026-02-20 — started deeper debugging (notes below).

Commands I ran (raw outputs, trimmed):
1) Basic connectivity from customer bastion -> service IP (10.20.5.12)
$ ping -c3 10.20.5.12
PING 10.20.5.12 (10.20.5.12): 56 data bytes
--- 10.20.5.12 ping statistics ---
3 packets transmitted, 0 packets received, 100% packet loss

2) traceroute from customer -> our LB (shows drop at peering):
$ traceroute -n 10.20.5.12
1  10.0.1.1  1.2 ms  1.1 ms  1.2 ms
2  10.0.2.1  2.3 ms  2.1 ms  2.2 ms
3  * * *

3) From infra jump host in our VPC -> customer IP (10.20.0.0/16):
$ ip route get 10.20.5.12
10.20.5.12 via 10.0.3.2 dev eth0 src 10.0.3.5 uid 0

4) Check VPC peering and route tables (aws cli):
$ aws ec2 describe-vpc-peering-connections --filters "Name=status-code,Values=active" | jq -r '.VpcPeeringConnections[] | {VpcPeeringConnectionId: .VpcPeeringConnectionId,RequesterVpcInfo: .RequesterVpcInfo.CidrBlock,AccepterVpcInfo: .AccepterVpcInfo.CidrBlock}'
{"VpcPeeringConnectionId":"pcx-0abc1234","RequesterVpcInfo":"10.0.0.0/16","AccepterVpcInfo":"10.20.0.0/16"}

$ aws ec2 describe-route-tables --filters Name=association.subnet-id,Values=subnet-0a1b2c | jq -r '.RouteTables[] | .Routes[]'
# Found: route with DestinationCidrBlock 10.20.0.0/16 target pcx-0abc1234
# BUT: noticed another route in a different RT that has an overlapping more-specific 10.20.5.0/24 pointed to a NAT gateway (nat-0aaa) -> causes asymmetric routing for pod egress

5) DNS checks from customer side (resolves to public IP unexpectedly):
$ dig +short model.internal.redwood.example.com @10.0.2.2
203.0.113.45

- That public IP goes to our hosted API front door (which expects auth & different TLS cert). So customer tries to reach internal model IP but DNS returns public front-door. Suspect split-horizon DNS misconfiguration or conditional forwarder missing.

6) TLS handshake check (from customer bastion to the public IP returned by DNS):
$ openssl s_client -connect 203.0.113.45:443 -servername model.internal.redwood.example.com -brief -showcerts 2>/dev/null | sed -n '1,120p'
CONNECTED(00000003)
1397045:error:1408F10B:SSL routines:ssl3_get_record:wrong version number:../ssl/record/rec_layer_s3.c:353
---
No peer certificate available

- When connecting directly to internal IP (10.20.5.12) with s_client SNI same name -> TLS handshake starts but then gets RST at 1st application record. Hypothesis: SNI mismatch, and our LB (in public path) is terminating TLS and returning client-facing cert causing client to fail (client expects internal cert).

7) tcpdump on our internal LB (short):
$ sudo tcpdump -nni eth0 host 10.20.5.12 and port 443 -c 50 -w /tmp/cap.pcap
# Observed: SYN from customer -> SYN/ACK from our node, then client sends ACK then immediately RST from customer IP. In other runs we saw SYNs not reaching our nodes at all.

Debug hypotheses (ranked):
- H1: Route tables overlap / more-specific route to NAT in the customer's associated subnet causes asymmetric routing: packets go customer->our VPC via peering, but return path hits NAT/igw and drops. Evidence: route table had 10.20.5.0/24 -> nat-0aaa.
- H2: Split-horizon DNS not configured or conditional forwarders lost after route cleanup: customer DNS resolved internal host to public front-door. Evidence: dig returned public IP.
- H3: TLS termination mismatch when traffic hits public front-door (cert mismatch) because SNI rewritten or public LB handles the name. Evidence: openssl errors, public IP.
- H4: Security group / NACL denies ephemeral ports on one side leading to half-open connections (less likely but possible).

Immediate actions taken (and results):
- Re-applied route for 10.20.5.0/24 to point at peering (replaced NAT). Result: some pings started succeeding (~30% success).
- Added missing conditional forwarder on our DNS side for customer domain: bind zones updated to serve 10.20.x for model.internal.redwood.example.com -> now resolves to 10.20.5.12 for bastion.
- Temp fix: added route in customer route table to force 10.0.0.0/16 via pcx-0abc1234. Result: larger recovery of healthchecks.

Open questions / next steps:
- Why did route cleanup PR create the more-specific 10.20.5.0/24 -> NAT route? Was it auto-generated or leftover from older migration? Need to check PR diff and rt associations. (Related: PR #221).
- Confirm whether the public front-door is configured to rewrite SNI when proxying to internal backends. If so, need to update to preserve SNI or configure internal TLS to accept front-door cert.
- Need an incident postmortem draft: who touched route tables during maintenance, why conditional DNS forwarder got removed.

To-dos (short):
- [ ] Audit route-table associations across all subnets touched in PR #221 (assign: Eliot).
- [ ] Add automated tests for conditional forwarder existence during infra deploy (assign: me).
- [ ] Confirm with infra-net team whether NAT -> peering more-specific routes are expected (assign: Noah).
- [ ] Add logging to LB to capture SNI header/ClientHello for failed handshakes (assign: infra-ops).

Notes to self (fragile, scratch):
- Watch for asymmetric routing patterns: traceroute that stops at hop 3 often means missing peering route or NACL.
- When dig returns a public IP for an internal name, check both: BIND zones on infra-dns and any conditional forwarders in customer DNS servers.
- TLS: openssl errors like "wrong version number" often mean plain HTTP on that port or TLS handshake failure due to instrumentation (e.g., ALB doing TCP->TLS translation).

Helpful references / commands to repeat when I pick this up again:
- aws ec2 describe-route-tables --filters "Name=vpc-id,Values=<vpc-id>" | jq .
- dig +trace model.internal.redwood.example.com
- sudo tcpdump -nni any host <ip> and port 443 -w /tmp/trace.pcap
- openssl s_client -connect <ip>:443 -servername model.internal.redwood.example.com -alpn h2

Low-priority followups:
- Add monitoring alert when internal host resolves to non-private IPs in production (DNS drift).
- Create runbook checklist for maintenance windows touching route tables: include DNS forwarder validation and peering route sanity check.

End of file.
